lessons.title: Reach for the top
yt: class 9 english reach for the top

blocks.x: Two inspiring life stories. Part I is about Santosh Yadav, the mountaineer from Haryana who climbed Mount Everest twice, in 1992 and 1993, and was the first woman to do so. Part II is about Maria Sharapova, the Russian tennis player who left home as a child to train in the USA and won Wimbledon at the age of seventeen.
Deep dive: Santosh Yadav

Santosh Yadav, from Haryana, loved the mountains and trained as a mountaineer. She climbed Mount Everest in 1992 and again in 1993 and became the first woman to do it twice. Her climbs show that courage and discipline can overcome fear and hardship. She was honoured for her achievements.
Deep dive: Maria Sharapova

Maria Sharapova was born in Russia in 1987. As a young girl she showed great talent for tennis, and her father took her to the United States to train. Life was hard, but she worked with great determination. In 2004, at the age of seventeen, she won the Wimbledon title by defeating Serena Williams.
Deep dive: message
Both women set high goals, worked hard, accepted sacrifices and reached the top. The chapter encourages young people to follow their dreams.

Santosh Yadav ne Everest ko do baar fateh kiya. Maria Sharapova ne 17 saal me Wimbledon jita.
Courage, hard work and determination lead to the top.

Santosh Yadav

  • Santosh Yadav, from Haryana, loved the mountains and trained as a mountaineer
  • She climbed Mount Everest in 1992 and again in 1993 and became the first woman to do it twice
  • Her climbs show that courage and discipline can overcome fear and hardship
  • She was honoured for her achievements
🧠

Maria Sharapova

  • Maria Sharapova was born in Russia in 1987
  • As a young girl she showed great talent for tennis, and her father took her to the United States to train
  • Life was hard, but she worked with great determination
  • In 2004, at the age of seventeen, she won the Wimbledon title by defeating Serena Williams
🌟

Message

  • Both women set high goals, worked hard, accepted sacrifices and reached the top
  • The chapter encourages young people to follow their dreams

blocks.x: A true story by Kenneth Anderson about a sloth bear cub named Bruno that the family adopted. The family fed him from a bottle, he became a playful and affectionate pet, and he grew very attached to them. The story shows the love between humans and animals, and the sadness of parting when the animal grew too big to be kept at home.
Deep dive: story

The Anderson family adopts a sloth bear cub and names him Bruno. They feed him milk from a bottle and care for him like a child. Bruno becomes a funny and loving pet who follows them around. As he grows bigger and stronger he can no longer be kept safely at home. The family is sad to let him go.
Deep dive: message
Animals feel love and attachment just like humans, and kindness is returned with love. A wild animal belongs to nature, and sometimes love means letting go.
Hindi saransh
Anderson parivar ek bhaalu ke bachche Bruno ko paalta hai; unke beech pyaar ka rishta ban jata hai.
Love between humans and animals is real and lasting.

lessons.title: Kathmandu

blocks.x: A travel account by the Indian writer Vikram Seth. He visits Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal, and describes two famous places: the Hindu temple of Pashupatinath and the Buddhist stupa of Boudhanath. He sees the crowds, hears the temple bells, and notes how Hindu and Buddhist practices live side by side.
Deep dive: places

Vikram Seth describes Kathmandu's Pashupatinath temple, a Hindu shrine of Lord Shiva near the Bagmati river, and Boudhanath, a large Buddhist stupa. He notes crowds of worshippers, the sound of bells, the offerings and the smells of incense.
Deep dive: theme
The chapter shows how Hindu and Buddhist traditions coexist in Kathmandu. It also shows that travel writing observes people, places and culture with curiosity and respect.
Hindi saransh
Vikram Seth Kathmandu ke Pashupatinath mandir aur Boudhanath stupa ka varnan karte hain.
Kathmandu shows how two faiths can share space in harmony.

lessons.html:
Visual lesson

Kathmandu

A travel account by the Indian writer Vikram Seth

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Places›3Theme
🔑

Big idea

  • A travel account by the Indian writer Vikram Seth
  • He visits Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal, and describes two famous places: the Hindu temple of Pashupatinath and the Buddhist stupa of Boudhanath
  • He sees the crowds, hears the temple bells, and notes how Hindu and Buddhist practices live side by side
📌

Places

  • Vikram Seth describes Kathmandu's Pashupatinath temple, a Hindu shrine of Lord Shiva near the Bagmati river, and Boudhanath, a large Buddhist stupa
  • He notes crowds of worshippers, the sound of bells, the offerings and the smells of incense
🧠

Theme

  • The chapter shows how Hindu and Buddhist traditions coexist in Kathmandu
  • It also shows that travel writing observes people, places and culture with curiosity and respect
🧮

Formula tiles

AuthorVikram SethIndian writer
CityKathmanduNepal
SitesPashupatinath, BoudhanathHindu, Buddhist
Themeharmonyfaith
🎯 Remember Kathmandu shows how two faiths can share space in harmony.
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

Vikram Seth Kathmandu ke Pashupatinath mandir aur Boudhanath stupa ka varnan karte hain.

lessons.title: If I were you
yt: class 9 english if i were you

blocks.x: A one-act play by Douglas James. An intruder, a criminal, enters a house planning to kill its owner and take his place. The owner stays calm, outwits the intruder with clever talk and the police finally arrive and arrest him. The play is a thriller built on suspense and quick wit.
Deep dive: plot

An intruder enters a house meaning to kill the owner and take his identity. The owner, instead of panicking, talks cleverly and keeps him engaged. As the play moves, the owner changes the situation in his favour. The police arrive and arrest the intruder.
Deep dive: devices
The play builds suspense through dialogue, uses irony and has few characters and one setting. It teaches that intelligence and calm are stronger than force.

Visual lesson

If I were you

A one-act play by Douglas James

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Plot›3Devices
🔑

Big idea

  • A one-act play by Douglas James
  • An intruder, a criminal, enters a house planning to kill its owner and take his place
  • The owner stays calm, outwits the intruder with clever talk and the police finally arrive and arrest him
  • The play is a thriller built on suspense and quick wit
📌

Plot

  • An intruder enters a house meaning to kill the owner and take his identity
  • The owner, instead of panicking, talks cleverly and keeps him engaged
  • As the play moves, the owner changes the situation in his favour
  • The police arrive and arrest the intruder
🧠

Devices

  • The play builds suspense through dialogue, uses irony and has few characters and one setting
  • It teaches that intelligence and calm are stronger than force
🧮

lessons.title: The road not taken
yt: class 9 english the road not taken

blocks.x: A poem by the American poet Robert Frost (1874 to 1963), first published in 1916 in the book Mountain Interval. The speaker stands where two roads divide in a yellow wood in autumn, chooses the one less travelled and says that this choice made all the difference.
Deep dive: meaning

A traveller in a yellow autumn wood comes to a fork. He looks down one path as far as he can, then takes the other, which seems grassy and less worn. Yet the two are really almost the same. He keeps the first for another day, knowing that he will probably never return. Years later he will say he took the road less travelled and that it made all the difference.
Deep dive: devices
The road is a metaphor for life choices. The poem uses imagery of the autumn wood, rhyme ABAAB, a reflective tone and a quiet ending. It suggests that people often explain their choices afterwards.
Hindi saransh
Kavi do raston me se kam chale gaye raste ko chunta hai aur kehta hai usne sab badal diya.
The choices we make shape our life.

Visual lesson

The road not taken

A poem by the American poet Robert Frost (1874 to 1963), first published in 1916 in the book Mountain Interval

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Meaning›3Devices
Year1916
Stanzas4 of 5 lines
🔑

Big idea

  • A poem by the American poet Robert Frost (1874 to 1963), first published in 1916 in the book Mountain Interval
  • The speaker stands where two roads divide in a yellow wood in autumn, chooses the one less travelled and says that this choice made all the difference
📘

Meaning

  • A traveller in a yellow autumn wood comes to a fork
  • He looks down one path as far as he can, then takes the other, which seems grassy and less worn
  • Yet the two are really almost the same
  • He keeps the first for another day, knowing that he will probably never return
Read the full explanation

A traveller in a yellow autumn wood comes to a fork. He looks down one path as far as he can, then takes the other, which seems grassy and less worn. Yet the two are really almost the same. He keeps the first for another day, knowing that he will probably never return. Years later he will say he took the road less travelled and that it made all the difference.

🧠

Devices

  • The road is a metaphor for life choices
  • The poem uses imagery of the autumn wood, rhyme ABAAB, a reflective tone and a quiet ending
  • It suggests that people often explain their choices afterwards
🧮

lessons.title: Wind

blocks.x: A poem by the Tamil poet Subramania Bharati (1882 to 1921), translated into English. The poet asks the wind not to come too strongly. It breaks windows, shutters and doors, scatters papers and shakes houses and teaches that only the strong survive.
Deep dive: meaning

The poet speaks to the wind and asks it not to come too wildly. It breaks window shutters, scatters papers and books, pulls down roofs and snuffs out fires. The wind is a god that cannot be blamed. The poet tells us to build strong homes and strong hearts so that wind, the force of nature, becomes our friend and not our enemy.
Deep dive: devices
The poem uses personification, imagery of destruction, and a direct address. It suggests that life tests us, and only the strong will pass.
Hindi saransh
Hawa kamjoron ko todti hai aur mazbooton ko sahara deti hai.
Be strong and the wind will become your friend.

blocks.x: A poem by the American poet Coates Kinney (1826 to 1904). The speaker lies in bed under the roof and listens to the rain drumming overhead. The sound brings back sweet memories of childhood and of his mother, and he feels warm and happy in the cosy room.
Deep dive: meaning

The poet lies on his bed and hears the rain beat on the roof above him. The sound is like music, and he feels the past come alive: old friends, loving faces, and especially his mother. The memories are tender, joyful and a little sad. The simple sound turns into a bridge between present and past.
Deep dive: devices
The poem uses imagery of sound, a soothing rhythm, repetition and a nostalgic mood. It shows how a small sensory experience can open the heart.
Hindi saransh
Baarish ki aawaz kavi ko bachpan aur maa ki yaad dilati hai.
A simple sound can bring back dear memories.

lessons.title: The Lake Isle of Innisfree
yt: class 9 english the lake isle of innisfree

blocks.x: A poem by the Irish poet W. B. Yeats (1865 to 1939), first published in 1890. Living in busy London, the speaker longs to return to the peaceful island of Innisfree in Lough Gill, where he would build a small cabin, grow beans, keep bees and live in calm.
Deep dive: meaning

The speaker says he will rise and go to Innisfree, where he will build a small cabin and grow beans and keep bees. There he will find peace, which comes slowly from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings. He is standing on grey pavements in the city, but he hears the lake water in the deep of his heart.
Deep dive: devices
The poem uses vivid imagery of colour and sound, a contrast between city and nature, repetition of "I will arise and go now" and a longing tone. It shows the human desire for peace in a busy world.
Hindi saransh
London ke shor me kavi Innisfree ke shant dweep par jana chahta hai.
Peace is found in nature, not in the noisy city.

Visual lesson

The Lake Isle of Innisfree

A poem by the Irish poet W

minutes
formulas
Q&A

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Meaning›3Devices
Year1890
🔑

Big idea

  • A poem by the Irish poet W
  • Yeats (1865 to 1939), first published in 1890
  • Living in busy London, the speaker longs to return to the peaceful island of Innisfree in Lough Gill, where he would build a small cabin, grow beans…
📘

Meaning

  • The speaker says he will rise and go to Innisfree, where he will build a small cabin and grow beans and keep bees
  • There he will find peace, which comes slowly from the veils of the morning to where the cricket sings
  • He is standing on grey pavements in the city, but he hears the lake water in the deep of his heart
🧠

Devices

  • The poem uses vivid imagery of colour and sound, a contrast between city and nature, repetition of "I will arise and go now" and a longing tone
  • It shows the human desire for peace in a busy world
🧮

Formula tiles

PoetW. B. YeatsIrish
PlaceInnisfreeLough Gill
Themepeace in naturelonging
🎯 Remember Peace is found in nature, not in the noisy city.

London ke shor me kavi Innisfree ke shant dweep par jana chahta hai.

blocks.x: A ballad by the American poet Phoebe Cary (1824 to 1871). Saint Peter visits a village and asks an old woman for food. She bakes a cake for him, but each time she thinks it is too big, she bakes a smaller one. In the end she refuses and is turned into a woodpecker. The poem warns against greed and selfishness.
Deep dive: story

Saint Peter, in disguise, visits an old woman and asks for something to eat. She puts a little dough in the oven, but the cake comes out too large, so she makes a smaller one. This happens again and again. At last she refuses to give him anything. As punishment she is turned into a woodpecker who must peck for food for ever.
Deep dive: devices
The poem is a ballad with a narrative style, a magical transformation and a clear moral. It uses repetition to show the woman's greed grow.
Hindi saransh
Lalchi budhiya ko sant ki seva se mana karne par chidiya bana diya gaya.
Greed brings punishment; generosity brings blessing.

lessons.html:
Visual lesson

A legend of the Northland

A ballad by the American poet Phoebe Cary (1824 to 1871)

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Story›3Devices
🔑

Big idea

  • A ballad by the American poet Phoebe Cary (1824 to 1871)
  • Saint Peter visits a village and asks an old woman for food
  • She bakes a cake for him, but each time she thinks it is too big, she bakes a smaller one
  • In the end she refuses and is turned into a woodpecker
Read the full explanation

A ballad by the American poet Phoebe Cary (1824 to 1871). Saint Peter visits a village and asks an old woman for food. She bakes a cake for him, but each time she thinks it is too big, she bakes a smaller one. In the end she refuses and is turned into a woodpecker. The poem warns against greed and selfishness.

✍️

Story

  • Saint Peter, in disguise, visits an old woman and asks for something to eat
  • She puts a little dough in the oven, but the cake comes out too large, so she makes a smaller one
  • This happens again and again
  • At last she refuses to give him anything
Read the full explanation

Saint Peter, in disguise, visits an old woman and asks for something to eat. She puts a little dough in the oven, but the cake comes out too large, so she makes a smaller one. This happens again and again. At last she refuses to give him anything. As punishment she is turned into a woodpecker who must peck for food for ever.

🧠

Devices

  • The poem is a ballad with a narrative style, a magical transformation and a clear moral
  • It uses repetition to show the woman's greed grow
🧮

lessons.title: No men are foreign
yt: class 9 english no men are foreign

blocks.x: A poem by the English poet James Kirkup (1918 to 2009). It says that all human beings are alike and belong to one earth, breathe the same air and share the same sun. War and hatred are therefore wrong, and we should live as one family.
Deep dive: meaning

The poet says that no man is foreign. The same sun warms everyone, the same air is breathed by all, and the same earth holds all. People differ in language and country, but they are alike in blood and heart. War turns brothers into enemies and fills the earth with graves. The poet asks us to remember this and love one another.
Deep dive: devices
The poem uses repetition, simple direct language and images of nature to express brotherhood. It carries a strong anti-war message.
Hindi saransh
Sab manushya ek jaise hain; koi vidheshi nahi, isliye yuddh galat hai.
All human beings are one family.

1Big idea›2Meaning›3Devices
🔑

Big idea

  • A poem by the English poet James Kirkup (1918 to 2009)
  • It says that all human beings are alike and belong to one earth, breathe the same air and share the same sun
  • War and hatred are therefore wrong, and we should live as one family
📘

Meaning

  • The poet says that no man is foreign
  • The same sun warms everyone, the same air is breathed by all, and the same earth holds all
  • People differ in language and country, but they are alike in blood and heart
  • War turns brothers into enemies and fills the earth with graves
Read the full explanation

The poet says that no man is foreign. The same sun warms everyone, the same air is breathed by all, and the same earth holds all. People differ in language and country, but they are alike in blood and heart. War turns brothers into enemies and fills the earth with graves. The poet asks us to remember this and love one another.

🧠

Devices

  • The poem uses repetition, simple direct language and images of nature to express brotherhood
  • It carries a strong anti-war message
🧮

blocks.x: A poem by the Indian poet and painter Gieve Patel (1940 to 2023). It describes how hard it is to kill a tree. One has to hack it, uproot it, burn it and poison its roots before it finally dies. A tree is a living being that cannot be destroyed easily.
Deep dive: meaning

The poet says that killing a tree is not a quick or easy job. A tree has grown slowly in sun, air and earth for years. One must hack it with an axe, but it will survive. To destroy it completely the roots must be pulled out, exposed to the sun and air until they dry and turn brown, and only then does the tree die.
Deep dive: devices
The poem uses detailed imagery, personification, slow rhythm and a serious tone. It carries an environmental message about the value of trees.
Hindi saransh
Ped ko maarna aasan nahi; use jad se nasht karna padta hai.
Trees are strong; they deserve our protection.

lessons.title: A slumber did my spirit seal
yt: class 9 english a slumber did my spirit seal

blocks.x: A short poem by the English Romantic poet William Wordsworth (1770 to 1850), one of the Lucy poems. In two stanzas the speaker says that love once made him feel unaware of time and death. Now that Lucy is dead, she is part of the earth, rolled round with rocks and trees.
Deep dive: meaning

In the first stanza the speaker says a slumber sealed his spirit, so he did not fear the passage of time; Lucy seemed to him a thing that could not feel the touch of earthly years. In the second stanza she has died. She has no motion and no force, she neither hears nor sees, and she is rolled round in earth's daily course with rocks and stones and trees.
Deep dive: devices
The poem uses contrast between before and after, simple language and a calm tone. It is an elegy that shows how nature absorbs all life.
Hindi saransh
Kavi pyaar me samay aur mrityu ko bhool gaya tha; ab Lucy prakriti ka hissa ban chuki hai.
Death makes all things part of nature.

lessons.html:
Visual lesson

A slumber did my spirit seal

A short poem by the English Romantic poet William Wordsworth (1770 to 1850), one of the Lucy poems

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Meaning›3Devices
Stanzas2 of 4 lines
🔑

Big idea

  • A short poem by the English Romantic poet William Wordsworth (1770 to 1850), one of the Lucy poems
  • In two stanzas the speaker says that love once made him feel unaware of time and death
  • Now that Lucy is dead, she is part of the earth, rolled round with rocks and trees
📘

Meaning

  • In the first stanza the speaker says a slumber sealed his spirit, so he did not fear the passage of time
  • Lucy seemed to him a thing that could not feel the touch of earthly years
  • In the second stanza she has died
  • She has no motion and no force, she neither hears nor sees, and she is rolled round in earth's daily course with rocks and stones and trees
🧠

Devices

  • The poem uses contrast between before and after, simple language and a calm tone
  • It is an elegy that shows how nature absorbs all life
🧮

lessons.title: The lost child

blocks.x: A short story by the Indian writer Mulk Raj Anand. A small boy goes with his parents to a spring fair. He asks for sweets, toys, balloons and flowers, but they do not buy them, so he lags behind, looks at the shops, and is soon lost in the crowd. Frightened, he cries for his parents and in the end wants only them, not the toys.
Deep dive: story

A small boy goes with his parents to a spring fair in a village. He sees sweets, toys, balloons and flowers and begs for them. His parents move on and he lags behind, absorbed in the shops. Suddenly he finds himself alone in a crowd, panics and cries for his parents. Now toys and sweets mean nothing. He wants only to be with his mother and father.
Deep dive: message
The story shows that a child's deepest need is love and security. It also shows how easily a child can be lost in the world of attractions.
Hindi saransh
Mela me kho gaya bachcha khilaunon se zyada apne mata pita ko chahta hai.
Parents matter more than toys.

Visual lesson

The lost child

A short story by the Indian writer Mulk Raj Anand

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Story›3Message
🔑

Big idea

  • A short story by the Indian writer Mulk Raj Anand
  • A small boy goes with his parents to a spring fair
  • He asks for sweets, toys, balloons and flowers, but they do not buy them, so he lags behind, looks at the shops, and is soon lost in the crowd
  • Frightened, he cries for his parents and in the end wants only them, not the toys
✍️

Story

  • A small boy goes with his parents to a spring fair in a village
  • He sees sweets, toys, balloons and flowers and begs for them
  • His parents move on and he lags behind, absorbed in the shops
  • Suddenly he finds himself alone in a crowd, panics and cries for his parents
Read the full explanation

A small boy goes with his parents to a spring fair in a village. He sees sweets, toys, balloons and flowers and begs for them. His parents move on and he lags behind, absorbed in the shops. Suddenly he finds himself alone in a crowd, panics and cries for his parents. Now toys and sweets mean nothing. He wants only to be with his mother and father.

🧠

Message

  • The story shows that a child's deepest need is love and security
  • It also shows how easily a child can be lost in the world of attractions
🧮

lessons.title: The adventures of Toto
yt: class 9 english the adventures of toto

blocks.x: A humorous story by the Indian writer Ruskin Bond. His grandfather buys a mischievous little monkey named Toto for a few rupees and keeps him at home. Toto gets into all kinds of trouble, upsetting the family, especially Grandmother, but the grandfather keeps his affection for him.
Deep dive: story

The narrator's grandfather brings home a young monkey named Toto. The family finds him full of mischief and he keeps causing trouble. Grandmother does not approve, while Grandfather loves him. The story is told with warm humour and shows how a pet can bring both delight and disorder.
Deep dive: message
The story teaches kindness to animals and shows the love between a grandfather and his pet. It is a light, humorous account of life with a mischievous monkey.
Hindi saransh
Dada ji ek shararati bandar Toto laate hain jo ghar me kai musibaten khada karta hai.
Pets bring joy and trouble in equal measure.

lessons.title: Iswaran the storyteller

blocks.x: A short story by R. K. Narayan. Mahesh, the narrator, describes his cook Iswaran, who is a wonderful storyteller. His stories are full of ghosts and strange events and he says he has seen them. The narrator enjoys them even though he doubts that they are true.
Deep dive: story

Mahesh describes Iswaran, his cook, as a wonderful storyteller. Iswaran tells stories of ghosts and strange happenings and says that he has himself witnessed them. Mahesh listens with delight although he does not fully believe them. The story shows the humour and charm of ordinary people.
Deep dive: message
Imagination and storytelling make life more colourful. Narayan observes people with affection and gentle humour.
Hindi saransh
Iswaran ek ras bhara kahani sunane wala rasoiya hai jiski kahaniyan rochak hoti hain.
A good story-teller can hold anyone's attention.

lessons.title: In the kingdom of fools
yt: class 9 english in the kingdom of fools

blocks.x: A folk tale from Karnataka. A guru and his disciple arrive in a kingdom where everything, whether vegetables or sweets, is sold at the same price. The guru wants to leave but the greedy disciple wants to stay. The foolish king and his ministers bring trouble, and the guru finally saves the disciple by a clever trick.
Deep dive: story

A guru and his disciple travel to a strange kingdom where all things are priced the same. The guru senses danger and wants to go, but the greedy disciple loves the cheap food. The foolish king and ministers punish people without sense. The disciple lands in trouble and the guru rescues him with a clever plan.
Deep dive: message
The tale satirises foolish rulers and warns against greed. It shows that a wise person can save a friend from danger.
Hindi saransh
Murkhon ke rajya me guru apne lalchi shishya ko apni chaaturi se bachata hai.
Wisdom is better than greed.

Visual lesson

In the kingdom of fools

A folk tale from Karnataka

minutes
formulas

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Story›3Message
🔑

Big idea

  • A folk tale from Karnataka
  • A guru and his disciple arrive in a kingdom where everything, whether vegetables or sweets, is sold at the same price
  • The guru wants to leave but the greedy disciple wants to stay
  • The foolish king and his ministers bring trouble, and the guru finally saves the disciple by a clever trick
✍️

Story

  • A guru and his disciple travel to a strange kingdom where all things are priced the same
  • The guru senses danger and wants to go, but the greedy disciple loves the cheap food
  • The foolish king and ministers punish people without sense
  • The disciple lands in trouble and the guru rescues him with a clever plan
🧠

Message

  • The tale satirises foolish rulers and warns against greed
  • It shows that a wise person can save a friend from danger
🧮

Formula tiles

Charactersguru, discipleking

Morallisten to the wiseavoid folly
🎯 Remember Wisdom is better than greed.

lessons.title: The Happy Prince

blocks.x: A fairy tale by Oscar Wilde (1854 to 1900). A statue of the Happy Prince, covered with gold leaf, with sapphire eyes and a ruby on his sword, stands high above a city. A swallow delays his migration to Egypt and, at the Prince's request, carries the jewels and gold to poor people. The swallow dies of cold and the statue's leaden heart breaks. In the end an angel takes the heart and the dead bird to heaven.
Deep dive: story

The Happy Prince is a statue above the city, covered with gold leaf, with sapphire eyes and a ruby on his sword. A swallow stops under his feet on the way to Egypt. The Prince, who can see the misery of the poor, begs the swallow to take his ruby, then his sapphire eyes and then his gold to the needy. The swallow grows weak in the cold and dies at the Prince's feet; the leaden heart breaks. The ungrateful city melts the shabby statue but the heart will not melt. An angel carries the heart and the dead swallow to heaven.
Deep dive: message
The tale praises compassion, sacrifice and friendship, and criticises a society that ignores the poor.
Hindi saransh
Khushhaal rajkumar ki murti garibon ko apne ratn bhej deti hai aur dono swarg paate hain.
True happiness lies in giving.

A fairy tale by Oscar Wilde (1854 to 1900). A statue of the Happy Prince, covered with gold leaf, with sapphire eyes and a ruby on his sword, stands high above a city. A swallow delays his migration to Egypt and, at the Prince's request, carries the jewels and gold to poor people. The swallow dies of cold and the statue's leaden heart breaks. In the end an angel takes the heart and the dead bird to heaven.

✍️

Story

  • The Happy Prince is a statue above the city, covered with gold leaf, with sapphire eyes and a ruby on his sword
  • A swallow stops under his feet on the way to Egypt
  • The Prince, who can see the misery of the poor, begs the swallow to take his ruby, then his sapphire eyes and then his gold to the needy
  • The swallow grows weak in the cold and dies at the Prince's feet
Read the full explanation

The Happy Prince is a statue above the city, covered with gold leaf, with sapphire eyes and a ruby on his sword. A swallow stops under his feet on the way to Egypt. The Prince, who can see the misery of the poor, begs the swallow to take his ruby, then his sapphire eyes and then his gold to the needy. The swallow grows weak in the cold and dies at the Prince's feet; the leaden heart breaks. The ungrateful city melts the shabby statue but the heart will not melt. An angel carries the heart and the dead swallow to heaven.

🧠

Message

  • The tale praises compassion, sacrifice and friendship, and criticises a society that ignores the poor

lessons.title: The Last Leaf

blocks.x: A short story by the American writer O. Henry (William Sydney Porter). In Greenwich Village two young artists, Sue and Johnsy, share a studio. Johnsy falls ill with pneumonia and believes she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy outside her window. The old painter Behrman paints a leaf on the wall in the night. Johnsy recovers, but Behrman dies of pneumonia.
Deep dive: story

Sue and Johnsy live in Greenwich Village. When Johnsy falls ill with pneumonia she imagines that she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy outside her window. Sue tells old Behrman, who scoffs but is moved. On a stormy night the last leaf remains on the wall all night and through the next day. Johnsy takes it as a sign and regains her will to live. Sue then tells her that Behrman has died of pneumonia: he painted the leaf on the wall in the storm.
Deep dive: message
The painted leaf is Behrman's masterpiece: an act of selfless love. The story shows the power of hope and sacrifice.
Hindi saransh
Behrman ne diwar par patta banakar Johnsy ki jaan bachayi aur khud chal base.
Sacrifice is the greatest masterpiece.

Visual lesson

The Last Leaf

A short story by the American writer O

1Big idea›2Story›3Message
🔑

Big idea

  • A short story by the American writer O
  • Henry (William Sydney Porter)
  • In Greenwich Village two young artists, Sue and Johnsy, share a studio
  • Johnsy falls ill with pneumonia and believes she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy outside her window
Read the full explanation

A short story by the American writer O. Henry (William Sydney Porter). In Greenwich Village two young artists, Sue and Johnsy, share a studio. Johnsy falls ill with pneumonia and believes she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy outside her window. The old painter Behrman paints a leaf on the wall in the night. Johnsy recovers, but Behrman dies of pneumonia.

✍️

Story

  • Sue and Johnsy live in Greenwich Village
  • When Johnsy falls ill with pneumonia she imagines that she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy outside her window
  • Sue tells old Behrman, who scoffs but is moved
  • On a stormy night the last leaf remains on the wall all night and through the next day
Read the full explanation

Sue and Johnsy live in Greenwich Village. When Johnsy falls ill with pneumonia she imagines that she will die when the last leaf falls from the ivy outside her window. Sue tells old Behrman, who scoffs but is moved. On a stormy night the last leaf remains on the wall all night and through the next day. Johnsy takes it as a sign and regains her will to live. Sue then tells her that Behrman has died of pneumonia: he painted the leaf on the wall in the storm.

🧠

Message

  • The painted leaf is Behrman's masterpiece: an act of selfless love
  • The story shows the power of hope and sacrifice

lessons.title: A house is not a home
yt: class 9 english a house is not a home

blocks.x: A story by Zan Gaudioso. It shows that a home is not made of walls and furniture but of the love and warmth of the people who live in it. When a house is lost, the family realises that what matters is being together.
Deep dive: story

The story reflects on what makes a house a home. The family loses or leaves the house but finds that they are still a home so long as they are together. Walls, roofs and furniture can be replaced, but love and family ties cannot.
Deep dive: message
A home is created by people, not by buildings. The story urges us to cherish loved ones.
Hindi saransh
Ghar eent patthar se nahi, pyaar aur parivar se banta hai.
Home is where the family is.

Big idea

  • A story by Zan Gaudioso
  • It shows that a home is not made of walls and furniture but of the love and warmth of the people who live in it
  • When a house is lost, the family realises that what matters is being together
✍️

Story

  • The story reflects on what makes a house a home
  • The family loses or leaves the house but finds that they are still a home so long as they are together
  • Walls, roofs and furniture can be replaced, but love and family ties cannot
🧠

Message

  • A home is created by people, not by buildings
  • The story urges us to cherish loved ones

lessons.title: The Accidental Tourist

blocks.x: A humorous essay by the American travel writer Bill Bryson. He recounts the funny mishaps and awkward moments that he faces as a traveller, from airports to hotels, and laughs at himself. He shows that travel is full of surprises, many of them embarrassing.
Deep dive: essay

Bill Bryson tells of the small disasters of a traveller: lost luggage, awkward manners, confusing places and unexpected events. He laughs at himself with exaggeration. The essay is light, easy to read and meant to make the reader smile.
Deep dive: message
Travel is full of unexpected incidents. A sense of humour makes them easier to bear.
Hindi saransh
Bill Bryson apne yatra ke hasyaspad anubhav sunate hain.
Laugh at your mishaps while travelling.

lessons.title: The Beggar

blocks.x: A short story by the Russian writer Anton Chekhov (1860 to 1904). A lawyer named Sergei meets a beggar, Lushkoff, who claims to be a former teacher. Sergei offers him wood-chopping work to earn his food. The cook Olga helps him and encourages him to change. Years later the beggar has reformed and gratefully thanks Olga.
Deep dive: story

Sergei, a lawyer, meets a beggar called Lushkoff and gives him wood to chop. Lushkoff is unwilling. Olga, the cook, takes pity on him, helps him chop the wood and talks to him kindly. Moved by her kindness, he changes his ways and finds honest work. Years later he meets Sergei again as a reformed man and thanks Olga.
Deep dive: message
Kindness and encouragement can change a person's life. Charity should give people dignity as well as money.

Bhikhari Lushkoff mehnat karna seekhta hai aur Olga ki dayalu madad se naya jeevan paata hai.
Kindness can change a life.

lessons.title: India: size and location
yt: class 9 geography india: size and location

blocks.x: India lies in the northern hemisphere between latitudes 8 degree 4 minute N and 37 degree 6 minute N and longitudes 68 degree 7 minute E and 97 degree 25 minute E. The Tropic of Cancer divides the country almost in half. Area is 3.28 million sq km, about 2.4 percent of the world, the seventh largest country. The Indian Standard Time is based on the 82 degree 30 minute E meridian. The Suez Canal made India closer to Europe.
Deep dive: location and extent

India lies entirely in the northern and eastern hemispheres. The mainland extends from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Arunachal Pradesh to Gujarat. The mainland lies between 8 degree 4 minute N and 37 degree 6 minute N, but the Indira Point in the Great Nicobar reaches 6 degree 45 minute N. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, so the northern half is in the temperate zone and the southern half in the tropical zone. With a land frontier of 15200 km and a coastline of 7516.6 km, India is a vital link between East and West.
Deep dive: time

The earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, so places 15 degrees apart differ by one hour and each degree is 4 minutes. The sun rises two hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in Gujarat. To avoid confusion, the 82 degree 30 minute E meridian near Naini (Prayagraj) is the Indian Standard Time, which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.
Deep dive: India and the world

The Indian Ocean gives India a central position between West Asia, Africa and Europe on one side and South-East and East Asia on the other. Deccan Peninsula extends into the Indian Ocean. After the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 the distance to Europe fell by about 7000 km. India has been in contact with the world through land routes and mountain passes since ancient times, which enriched Indian culture. Neighbours: Pakistan and Afghanistan in the north-west, China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north, Myanmar and Bangladesh in the east; Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours.

India lies in the northern hemisphere between latitudes 8 degree 4 minute N and 37 degree 6 minute N and longitudes 68 degree 7 minute E and 97 degree 25 minute E. The Tropic of Cancer divides the country almost in half. Area is 3.28 million sq km, about 2.4 percent of the world, the seventh largest country. The Indian Standard Time is based on the 82 degree 30 minute E meridian. The Suez Canal made India closer to Europe.

📌

Location and extent

  • India lies entirely in the northern and eastern hemispheres
  • The mainland extends from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Arunachal Pradesh to Gujarat
  • The mainland lies between 8 degree 4 minute N and 37 degree 6 minute N, but the Indira Point in the Great Nicobar reaches 6 degree 45 minute N

Read the full explanation

India lies entirely in the northern and eastern hemispheres. The mainland extends from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Arunachal Pradesh to Gujarat. The mainland lies between 8 degree 4 minute N and 37 degree 6 minute N, but the Indira Point in the Great Nicobar reaches 6 degree 45 minute N. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, so the northern half is in the temperate zone and the southern half in the tropical zone. With a land frontier of 15200 km and a coastline of 7516.6 km, India is a vital link between East and West.

🧠

Time

  • The earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, so places 15 degrees apart differ by one hour and each degree is 4 minutes
  • The sun rises two hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh than in Gujarat
  • To avoid confusion, the 82 degree 30 minute E meridian near Naini (Prayagraj) is the Indian Standard Time, which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of…
🌟

India and the world

  • The Indian Ocean gives India a central position between West Asia, Africa and Europe on one side and South-East and East Asia on the other
  • Deccan Peninsula extends into the Indian Ocean
  • After the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 the distance to Europe fell by about 7000 km
  • India has been in contact with the world through land routes and mountain passes since ancient times, which enriched Indian culture
Read the full explanation

The Indian Ocean gives India a central position between West Asia, Africa and Europe on one side and South-East and East Asia on the other. Deccan Peninsula extends into the Indian Ocean. After the opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 the distance to Europe fell by about 7000 km. India has been in contact with the world through land routes and mountain passes since ancient times, which enriched Indian culture. Neighbours: Pakistan and Afghanistan in the north-west, China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north, Myanmar and Bangladesh in the east; Sri Lanka and the Maldives are island neighbours.

lessons.title: Physical features of India
yt: class 9 geography physical features of india

blocks.x: India has a variety of physical features: the Himalayan mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. The Himalayas are young fold mountains made when the Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate. They have three parallel ranges: Himadri, Himachal and Shiwaliks. The Northern Plains are made of alluvium from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.
Deep dive: the Himalayas

The Himalayas stretch 2400 km from the Indus to the Brahmaputra, about 400 km wide in Kashmir and 150 km in Arunachal Pradesh. The Himadri (Greater Himalayas) is the most continuous range with an average height of 6000 m and contains the highest peaks, including Kanchenjunga. The Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) is 3700 to 4500 m high and has ranges such as Pir Panjal and the hill stations Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital. The Shiwaliks (900 to 1100 m) are made of unconsolidated sediments, with the duns such as Dehradun between them and the Himachal. The Purvanchal hills (Patkai, Naga, Manipur and Mizo hills) lie in the east.
Deep dive: plains, plateau and desert

The Northern Plains (about 7 lakh sq km) are formed of alluvium from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra, running 2400 km east to west. They have Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar and Khadar, and are the most fertile and densely populated region. The Peninsular Plateau is an old, stable block, with the Central Highlands north of the Narmada and the Deccan Plateau south of it, bounded by the Western Ghats (continuous) and Eastern Ghats (broken). The Thar Desert has barchans and receives less than 150 mm of rain.
Deep dive: coasts and islands

The western coastal plain is narrow, divided into Konkan, Kannad and Malabar coasts. The eastern plain is wider with deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, divided into the Northern Circar and the Coromandel coast. Lakshadweep, made of coral, has about 36 islands. The Andaman and Nicobar are bigger, more numerous and scattered, and include the active volcano Barren Island.

Physical features of India

India has a variety of physical features: the Himalayan mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands

Read the full explanation

India has a variety of physical features: the Himalayan mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. The Himalayas are young fold mountains made when the Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate. They have three parallel ranges: Himadri, Himachal and Shiwaliks. The Northern Plains are made of alluvium from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.

📌

The Himalayas

  • The Himalayas stretch 2400 km from the Indus to the Brahmaputra, about 400 km wide in Kashmir and 150 km in Arunachal Pradesh
  • The Himadri (Greater Himalayas) is the most continuous range with an average height of 6000 m and contains the highest peaks, including Kanchenjunga
  • The Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) is 3700 to 4500 m high and has ranges such as Pir Panjal and the hill stations Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital
  • The Shiwaliks (900 to 1100 m) are made of unconsolidated sediments, with the duns such as Dehradun between them and the Himachal
Read the full explanation

The Himalayas stretch 2400 km from the Indus to the Brahmaputra, about 400 km wide in Kashmir and 150 km in Arunachal Pradesh. The Himadri (Greater Himalayas) is the most continuous range with an average height of 6000 m and contains the highest peaks, including Kanchenjunga. The Himachal (Lesser Himalayas) is 3700 to 4500 m high and has ranges such as Pir Panjal and the hill stations Shimla, Mussoorie and Nainital. The Shiwaliks (900 to 1100 m) are made of unconsolidated sediments, with the duns such as Dehradun between them and the Himachal. The Purvanchal hills (Patkai, Naga, Manipur and Mizo hills) lie in the east.

🧠

Plains, plateau and desert

  • The Northern Plains (about 7 lakh sq km) are formed of alluvium from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra, running 2400 km east to west
  • They have Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar and Khadar, and are the most fertile and densely populated region
  • The Peninsular Plateau is an old, stable block, with the Central Highlands north of the Narmada and the Deccan Plateau south of it, bounded by the…
  • The Thar Desert has barchans and receives less than 150 mm of rain
Read the full explanation

The Northern Plains (about 7 lakh sq km) are formed of alluvium from the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra, running 2400 km east to west. They have Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar and Khadar, and are the most fertile and densely populated region. The Peninsular Plateau is an old, stable block, with the Central Highlands north of the Narmada and the Deccan Plateau south of it, bounded by the Western Ghats (continuous) and Eastern Ghats (broken). The Thar Desert has barchans and receives less than 150 mm of rain.

🌟

Coasts and islands

  • The western coastal plain is narrow, divided into Konkan, Kannad and Malabar coasts
  • The eastern plain is wider with deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, divided into the Northern Circar and the Coromandel coast
  • Lakshadweep, made of coral, has about 36 islands
  • The Andaman and Nicobar are bigger, more numerous and scattered, and include the active volcano Barren Island
Read the full explanation

The western coastal plain is narrow, divided into Konkan, Kannad and Malabar coasts. The eastern plain is wider with deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, divided into the Northern Circar and the Coromandel coast. Lakshadweep, made of coral, has about 36 islands. The Andaman and Nicobar are bigger, more numerous and scattered, and include the active volcano Barren Island.

lessons.title: Drainage

blocks.x: Drainage means the river system of an area. India has the Himalayan rivers (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra), which are perennial and fed by rain and snow, and the Peninsular rivers (Narmada, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri), which are seasonal and rain-fed. The Ganga is the longest river of India. Rivers form deltas, lakes and waterfalls.
Deep dive: Himalayan rivers

The Indus rises near Mansarovar in Tibet, flows west through Ladakh and Pakistan and falls in the Arabian Sea, length about 2900 km. The Ganga rises at Gangotri as the Bhagirathi, meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag, enters the plains at Haridwar and flows 2525 km to the Bay of Bengal, forming the Sundarbans delta with the Brahmaputra. The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet as the Tsangpo, enters India as the Dihang, forms the Majuli island and floods Assam and Bangladesh.
Deep dive: peninsular rivers

The Narmada and Tapi flow west in rift valleys and form estuaries. The Godavari (1465 km, Dakshin Ganga), Krishna, Kaveri and Mahanadi flow east and form deltas. Peninsular rivers are seasonal, have shorter and shallower courses and flow in fixed beds.
Deep dive: lakes and river pollution

Lakes are formed by glaciers, wind, river action and humans. Wular (Kashmir) is the largest freshwater lake, Dal is in Srinagar, Sambhar is a salt water lake, and Chilika is a lagoon on the Odisha coast. Rivers are polluted by sewage and industrial waste. The Ganga Action Plan (1985) and the National River Conservation Plan (1995) aim to clean them.

🔑

Big idea

  • Drainage means the river system of an area
  • India has the Himalayan rivers (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra), which are perennial and fed by rain and snow, and the Peninsular rivers (Narmada…
  • The Ganga is the longest river of India
  • Rivers form deltas, lakes and waterfalls
🗺️

Himalayan rivers

  • The Indus rises near Mansarovar in Tibet, flows west through Ladakh and Pakistan and falls in the Arabian Sea, length about 2900 km
  • The Ganga rises at Gangotri as the Bhagirathi, meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag, enters the plains at Haridwar and flows 2525 km to the Bay of…
  • The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet as the Tsangpo, enters India as the Dihang, forms the Majuli island and floods Assam and Bangladesh
Read the full explanation

The Indus rises near Mansarovar in Tibet, flows west through Ladakh and Pakistan and falls in the Arabian Sea, length about 2900 km. The Ganga rises at Gangotri as the Bhagirathi, meets the Alaknanda at Devprayag, enters the plains at Haridwar and flows 2525 km to the Bay of Bengal, forming the Sundarbans delta with the Brahmaputra. The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet as the Tsangpo, enters India as the Dihang, forms the Majuli island and floods Assam and Bangladesh.

🗺️

Peninsular rivers

  • The Narmada and Tapi flow west in rift valleys and form estuaries
  • The Godavari (1465 km, Dakshin Ganga), Krishna, Kaveri and Mahanadi flow east and form deltas
  • Peninsular rivers are seasonal, have shorter and shallower courses and flow in fixed beds
🗺️

Lakes and river pollution

  • Lakes are formed by glaciers, wind, river action and humans
  • Wular (Kashmir) is the largest freshwater lake, Dal is in Srinagar, Sambhar is a salt water lake, and Chilika is a lagoon on the Odisha coast
  • Rivers are polluted by sewage and industrial waste
  • The Ganga Action Plan (1985) and the National River Conservation Plan (1995) aim to clean them

lessons.title: Climate

blocks.x: India has a tropical monsoon climate. Weather is the day to day condition of the atmosphere, and climate is the average over a long period. Factors affecting climate are latitude, altitude, pressure and winds, distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief. There are four seasons: cold weather, hot weather, advancing monsoon and retreating monsoon.
Deep dive: controlling factors

Latitude: the Tropic of Cancer divides India, so the south is hot and the north is cooler. Altitude: temperature falls about 6.5 degrees per 1000 m, so hills are cooler. Pressure and winds: the system of the sub-continent, with seasonal reversal of winds. Distance from the sea: coastal places have a moderate climate and interior places have extremes. Relief: the Himalayas block the cold winds and the Western Ghats cause rain on the windward side.
Deep dive: monsoon and seasons

The summer heating of land causes low pressure over the north-west, which draws moist south-west winds from the Indian Ocean. They burst on the Kerala coast around 1 June and cover the country by mid-July, bringing most of the rain (about 75 percent). In winter the cold weather is clear with western disturbances. Hot weather has loo, mango showers and Kalbaisakhi. In the retreating monsoon the sky clears and the Tamil Nadu coast receives rain from the north-east winds.
Deep dive: importance
The monsoon is the pulse of Indian farming and the economy. Delay or failure causes drought, and excess causes floods. The cycle of seasons unites the people of India culturally.

Visual lesson

Climate

India has a tropical monsoon climate

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Controlling factors›3Monsoon and seasons›4Importance
Monsoon onset1 June
🔑

Big idea

  • India has a tropical monsoon climate
  • Weather is the day to day condition of the atmosphere, and climate is the average over a long period
  • Factors affecting climate are latitude, altitude, pressure and winds, distance from the sea, ocean currents and relief
  • There are four seasons: cold weather, hot weather, advancing monsoon and retreating monsoon
📌

Controlling factors

  • Latitude: the Tropic of Cancer divides India, so the south is hot and the north is cooler
  • Altitude: temperature falls about 6.5 degrees per 1000 m, so hills are cooler
  • Pressure and winds: the system of the sub-continent, with seasonal reversal of winds
  • Distance from the sea: coastal places have a moderate climate and interior places have extremes
Read the full explanation

Latitude: the Tropic of Cancer divides India, so the south is hot and the north is cooler. Altitude: temperature falls about 6.5 degrees per 1000 m, so hills are cooler. Pressure and winds: the system of the sub-continent, with seasonal reversal of winds. Distance from the sea: coastal places have a moderate climate and interior places have extremes. Relief: the Himalayas block the cold winds and the Western Ghats cause rain on the windward side.

🧠

Monsoon and seasons

  • The summer heating of land causes low pressure over the north-west, which draws moist south-west winds from the Indian Ocean
  • They burst on the Kerala coast around 1 June and cover the country by mid-July, bringing most of the rain (about 75 percent)
  • In winter the cold weather is clear with western disturbances
  • Hot weather has loo, mango showers and Kalbaisakhi
Read the full explanation

The summer heating of land causes low pressure over the north-west, which draws moist south-west winds from the Indian Ocean. They burst on the Kerala coast around 1 June and cover the country by mid-July, bringing most of the rain (about 75 percent). In winter the cold weather is clear with western disturbances. Hot weather has loo, mango showers and Kalbaisakhi. In the retreating monsoon the sky clears and the Tamil Nadu coast receives rain from the north-east winds.

🌟

Importance

  • The monsoon is the pulse of Indian farming and the economy
  • Delay or failure causes drought, and excess causes floods
  • The cycle of seasons unites the people of India culturally

lessons.title: Natural vegetation and wildlife
yt: class 9 geography natural vegetation and wildlife

blocks.x: Natural vegetation depends on temperature, rainfall, soil and relief. India has tropical evergreen forests, tropical deciduous forests, thorny scrubs, montane forests and mangrove forests. India has about 8 percent of the world's species. Projects and reserves like Project Tiger and biosphere reserves protect wildlife.
Deep dive: forest types

Tropical evergreen forests grow where rainfall exceeds 200 cm with a short dry season, in the Western Ghats, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar, and the north-east. They are dense with tall trees such as rosewood, mahogany and ebony. Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are the most widespread, in 70 to 200 cm rainfall, with teak, sal, shisham, sandalwood and khair; they shed leaves in the dry season. Thorny forests, in less than 70 cm rainfall, have acacia, palms, euphorbia and cacti with long roots and thorns. Montane forests change with height: wet temperate, then coniferous such as pine, deodar and fir, and alpine. Mangroves grow on tidal coasts, with the Sundari tree in the Sundarbans.
Deep dive: wildlife

India has about 8.1 percent of the world's species: about 47000 species of plants and 89000 species of animals. The elephant lives in Assam, Karnataka and Kerala; the one-horned rhino in Assam and West Bengal; the Asiatic lion in Gir; the tiger in many forests including the Sundarbans; the camel in the Thar; and the yak, snow leopard and bear in the Himalayas. Vultures and other species are declining.
Deep dive: conservation

The Wildlife Protection Act (1972), Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant (1992), 18 biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries conserve nature. Deforestation, poaching and pollution are the main threats.

Visual lesson

Natural vegetation and wildlife

Natural vegetation depends on temperature, rainfall, soil and relief

🔑

Big idea

  • Natural vegetation depends on temperature, rainfall, soil and relief
  • India has tropical evergreen forests, tropical deciduous forests, thorny scrubs, montane forests and mangrove forests
  • India has about 8 percent of the world's species
  • Projects and reserves like Project Tiger and biosphere reserves protect wildlife
📌

Forest types

  • Tropical evergreen forests grow where rainfall exceeds 200 cm with a short dry season, in the Western Ghats, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar, and…
  • They are dense with tall trees such as rosewood, mahogany and ebony
  • Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are the most widespread, in 70 to 200 cm rainfall, with teak, sal, shisham, sandalwood and khair
  • They shed leaves in the dry season
Read the full explanation

Tropical evergreen forests grow where rainfall exceeds 200 cm with a short dry season, in the Western Ghats, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar, and the north-east. They are dense with tall trees such as rosewood, mahogany and ebony. Tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests are the most widespread, in 70 to 200 cm rainfall, with teak, sal, shisham, sandalwood and khair; they shed leaves in the dry season. Thorny forests, in less than 70 cm rainfall, have acacia, palms, euphorbia and cacti with long roots and thorns. Montane forests change with height: wet temperate, then coniferous such as pine, deodar and fir, and alpine. Mangroves grow on tidal coasts, with the Sundari tree in the Sundarbans.

🧠

Wildlife

  • India has about 8.1 percent of the world's species: about 47000 species of plants and 89000 species of animals
  • The elephant lives in Assam, Karnataka and Kerala
  • The one-horned rhino in Assam and West Bengal
  • The Asiatic lion in Gir
Read the full explanation

India has about 8.1 percent of the world's species: about 47000 species of plants and 89000 species of animals. The elephant lives in Assam, Karnataka and Kerala; the one-horned rhino in Assam and West Bengal; the Asiatic lion in Gir; the tiger in many forests including the Sundarbans; the camel in the Thar; and the yak, snow leopard and bear in the Himalayas. Vultures and other species are declining.

🌟

Conservation

  • The Wildlife Protection Act (1972), Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant (1992), 18 biosphere reserves, national parks and sanctuaries conserve…
  • Deforestation, poaching and pollution are the main threats

lessons.title: Population

blocks.x: Population is studied through size, distribution and composition. The Census of 2011 gave India a population of about 1.21 billion, which is 17.5 percent of the world. Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state, and Sikkim the least. Population changes through births, deaths and migration. India's National Population Policy of 2000 aims at family welfare and a stable population.
Deep dive: size and distribution

India's population in 2011 was 1,210,854,977, about 17.5 percent of the world, though India has only 2.4 percent of the area. Uttar Pradesh has about 200 million people, nearly 16 percent of the country. Density was 382 per sq km. Densely populated places are the plains, deltas and coasts with fertile soil and rainfall; sparsely populated places are mountains, deserts and forests such as Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Sikkim.
Deep dive: growth, migration and structure

Growth depends on birth rate, death rate and migration. Since 1921 the death rate has fallen faster than the birth rate, causing rapid growth. Migration may be internal or international, rural to urban, for work or education. Age groups: children 0-14, working 15-59 and aged 60 and above. Adolescents (10-19 years) are about one-fifth of the population. India's occupational structure shows a big primary sector, and health and sanitation need improvement.
Deep dive: policy

The National Population Policy 2000 aims to meet the needs of reproductive health care, reduce infant mortality, promote delayed marriage and achieve a stable population. Education of girls, health care and better quality of life are keys to controlling population.

Big idea

  • Population is studied through size, distribution and composition
  • The Census of 2011 gave India a population of about 1.21 billion, which is 17.5 percent of the world

Read the full explanation

Population is studied through size, distribution and composition. The Census of 2011 gave India a population of about 1.21 billion, which is 17.5 percent of the world. Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state, and Sikkim the least. Population changes through births, deaths and migration. India's National Population Policy of 2000 aims at family welfare and a stable population.

📌

Size and distribution

  • India's population in 2011 was 1,210,854,977, about 17.5 percent of the world, though India has only 2.4 percent of the area
  • Uttar Pradesh has about 200 million people, nearly 16 percent of the country
  • Density was 382 per sq km
  • Densely populated places are the plains, deltas and coasts with fertile soil and rainfall
Read the full explanation

India's population in 2011 was 1,210,854,977, about 17.5 percent of the world, though India has only 2.4 percent of the area. Uttar Pradesh has about 200 million people, nearly 16 percent of the country. Density was 382 per sq km. Densely populated places are the plains, deltas and coasts with fertile soil and rainfall; sparsely populated places are mountains, deserts and forests such as Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and Sikkim.

🧠

Growth, migration and structure

  • Growth depends on birth rate, death rate and migration
  • Since 1921 the death rate has fallen faster than the birth rate, causing rapid growth
  • Migration may be internal or international, rural to urban, for work or education
  • Age groups: children 0-14, working 15-59 and aged 60 and above
Read the full explanation

Growth depends on birth rate, death rate and migration. Since 1921 the death rate has fallen faster than the birth rate, causing rapid growth. Migration may be internal or international, rural to urban, for work or education. Age groups: children 0-14, working 15-59 and aged 60 and above. Adolescents (10-19 years) are about one-fifth of the population. India's occupational structure shows a big primary sector, and health and sanitation need improvement.

🌟

Policy

  • The National Population Policy 2000 aims to meet the needs of reproductive health care, reduce infant mortality, promote delayed marriage and achieve…
  • Education of girls, health care and better quality of life are keys to controlling population

🎯 Remember Population change = births, deaths, migration.

yt: class 9 hindi शब्द भेद: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया, अव्यय

blocks.x: विकार के आधार पर शब्द दो प्रकार के हैं: विकारी (संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया) और अविकारी या अव्यय। संज्ञा से नाम, सर्वनाम से संज्ञा की जगह, विशेषण से गुण, क्रिया से कार्य और अव्यय से बिना बदले रहने वाले शब्द का बोध होता है।
गहराई से समझें: संज्ञा और सर्वनाम

संज्ञा पाँच प्रकार की होती है: व्यक्तिवाचक (राम, दिल्ली), जातिवाचक (लड़का, नदी), भाववाचक (मिठास, बचपन), समूहवाचक (सेना, कक्षा) और द्रव्यवाचक (सोना, दूध)। सर्वनाम संज्ञा की पुनरावृत्ति से बचाते हैं और छह प्रकार के होते हैं।
गहराई से समझें: विशेषण और क्रिया

विशेषण जिसकी विशेषता बताता है वह विशेष्य कहलाता है। गुणवाचक (लाल, मीठा), परिमाणवाचक (थोड़ा, दो लीटर), संख्यावाचक (चार, पाँचवाँ) और सार्वनामिक (यह लड़का) इसके भेद हैं। क्रिया के रूप से कर्म, काल और वाच्य का बोध होता है।
गहराई से समझें: अव्यय
जिन शब्दों में लिंग, वचन या कारक से परिवर्तन नहीं होता वे अव्यय हैं: क्रियाविशेषण (यहाँ, अब), संबंधबोधक (के पास), समुच्चयबोधक (और, तथा) और विस्मयादिबोधक (वाह!, हाय!)।
Hindi saransh
शब्द के पाँच मुख्य भेद हैं: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया और अव्यय।
विकारी: संज्ञा, सर्वनाम, विशेषण, क्रिया। अविकारी: अव्यय।

qa.a: किसी विशेष व्यक्ति, वस्तु या स्थान का नाम.

qa.q: 'जातिवाचक संज्ञा' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: पूरी जाति का बोध कराने वाला नाम.

qa.q: 'समूहवाचक संज्ञा' का क्या अर्थ है?

'पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: बोलने वाले, सुनने वाले या जिसके बारे में बात हो उसके लिए.

qa.q: 'निश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: निश्चित वस्तु का बोध, जैसे यह, वह.

qa.q: 'अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: अनिश्चित का बोध, जैसे कोई, कुछ.

qa.q: 'संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: दो वाक्यों को जोड़ने वाला, जैसे जो-सो.

qa.q: 'प्रश्नवाचक सर्वनाम' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: प्रश्न पूछने के लिए, जैसे कौन, क्या.

qa.q: 'निजवाचक सर्वनाम' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: अपनेपन का बोध, जैसे आप, स्वयं.

qa.q: 'गुणवाचक विशेषण' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: गुण या दशा बताने वाला शब्द.

qa.q: 'परिमाणवाचक विशेषण' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: मात्रा या माप बताने वाला शब्द.

qa.q: 'संख्यावाचक विशेषण' का क्या अर्थ है?
'सार्वनामिक विशेषण' का क्या अर्थ है?

qa.q: 'प्रेरणार्थक क्रिया' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: दूसरे से काम करवाने वाली क्रिया.

qa.q: 'क्रियाविशेषण' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: क्रिया की विशेषता बताने वाला अव्यय.

qa.q: 'समुच्चयबोधक' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: दो शब्दों या वाक्यों को जोड़ने वाला अव्यय.

lessons.title: संधि

blocks.x: दो वर्णों के मेल से जो विकार उत्पन्न होता है उसे संधि कहते हैं। संधि के तीन भेद हैं: स्वर संधि, व्यंजन संधि और विसर्ग संधि। स्वर संधि के पाँच भेद हैं: दीर्घ, गुण, वृद्धि, यण और अयादि।
गहराई से समझें: स्वर संधि

दीर्घ: अ/आ + अ/आ = आ (विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय); इ/ई + इ/ई = ई; उ/ऊ + उ/ऊ = ऊ। गुण: अ/आ + इ/ई = ए (नर + इंद्र = नरेंद्र), + उ/ऊ = ओ (सूर्य + उदय = सूर्योदय)। वृद्धि: अ/आ + ए/ऐ = ऐ, + ओ/औ = औ (सदा + एव = सदैव)। यण: इ + अ = य (इति + आदि = इत्यादि)। अयादि: ए + अ = अय् (ने + अन = नयन)।
गहराई से समझें: व्यंजन और विसर्ग संधि

व्यंजन संधि में त् + ज = ज्ज (सत् + जन = सज्जन), त् + न = न्न (उत् + नति = उन्नति)। विसर्ग संधि में विसर्ग का ओ, र्, श्, स् आदि में बदलना होता है: मनः + हर = मनोहर, निः + चल = निश्चल, दुः + जन = दुर्जन।
Hindi saransh
संधि = मेल। तीन भेद: स्वर, व्यंजन, विसर्ग।
संधि-विच्छेद का अर्थ है जोड़े हुए शब्द को अलग करना।

Big idea

  • दो वर्णों के मेल से जो विकार उत्पन्न होता है उसे संधि कहते हैं। संधि के तीन भेद हैं: स्वर संधि, व्यंजन संधि और विसर्ग संधि। स्वर संधि के पाँच भेद…
📌

गहराई से समझें: स्वर संधि

  • दीर्घ: अ/आ + अ/आ = आ (विद्या + आलय = विद्यालय)
  • इ/ई + इ/ई = ई
  • उ/ऊ + उ/ऊ = ऊ। गुण: अ/आ + इ/ई = ए (नर + इंद्र = नरेंद्र), + उ/ऊ = ओ (सूर्य + उदय = सूर्योदय)। वृद्धि: अ/आ + ए/ऐ = ऐ, + ओ/औ = औ (सदा + एव = सदैव)। यण:…
🧠

गहराई से समझें: व्यंजन और विसर्ग संधि

  • व्यंजन संधि में त् + ज = ज्ज (सत् + जन = सज्जन), त् + न = न्न (उत् + नति = उन्नति)। विसर्ग संधि में विसर्ग का ओ, र्, श्, स् आदि में बदलना होता है:…
🧮

lessons.title: समास

blocks.x: दो या दो से अधिक शब्दों के मेल से बने संक्षिप्त शब्द को समास कहते हैं। समास के छह भेद हैं: अव्ययीभाव, तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, द्विगु, द्वंद्व और बहुव्रीहि। विग्रह का अर्थ है समस्त पद को अलग-अलग करके अर्थ स्पष्ट करना।
गहराई से समझें: समास के भेद

अव्ययीभाव: पहला पद अव्यय (यथासंभव, आजन्म, प्रतिदिन)। तत्पुरुष: कारक चिह्नों का लोप (जेबघड़ी=जेब में रखी घड़ी)। कर्मधारय: नीलकमल = नीला है जो कमल। द्विगु: पंचवटी = पाँच वटों का समाहार। द्वंद्व: भाई-बहन = भाई और बहन। बहुव्रीहि: लंबोदर = लंबा है उदर जिसका (गणेश)।
गहराई से समझें: पहचान
समास पहचानने के लिए पदों की प्रधानता देखें और विग्रह करके देखें कि दोनों पद मिलकर कोई नया अर्थ देते हैं या नहीं।
Hindi saransh
समास = संक्षेप। छह भेद। विग्रह = समस्त पद का खोलना।
पहचानो: पूर्वपद प्रधान=अव्ययीभाव, उत्तरपद प्रधान=तत्पुरुष, दोनों प्रधान=द्वंद्व, अन्य प्रधान=बहुव्रीहि।

Visual lesson

समास

दो या दो से अधिक शब्दों के मेल से बने संक्षिप्त शब्द को समास कहते हैं। समास के छह भेद हैं: अव्ययीभाव, तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, द्विगु, द्वंद्व और बहुव्रीहि। विग्रह का अर्थ है…

🔑

Big idea

  • दो या दो से अधिक शब्दों के मेल से बने संक्षिप्त शब्द को समास कहते हैं। समास के छह भेद हैं: अव्ययीभाव, तत्पुरुष, कर्मधारय, द्विगु, द्वंद्व और…
📌

गहराई से समझें: समास के भेद

  • अव्ययीभाव: पहला पद अव्यय (यथासंभव, आजन्म, प्रतिदिन)। तत्पुरुष: कारक चिह्नों का लोप (जेबघड़ी=जेब में रखी घड़ी)। कर्मधारय: नीलकमल = नीला है जो कमल।…
🧠

गहराई से समझें: पहचान

  • समास पहचानने के लिए पदों की प्रधानता देखें और विग्रह करके देखें कि दोनों पद मिलकर कोई नया अर्थ देते हैं या नहीं।
🧮

Formula tiles

द्वंद्वदोनों प्रधानमाता-पिता

🎯 Remember पहचानो: पूर्वपद प्रधान=अव्ययीभाव, उत्तरपद प्रधान=तत्पुरुष, दोनों प्रधान=द्वंद्व, अन्य प्रधान=बहुव्रीहि।
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

समास = संक्षेप। छह भेद। विग्रह = समस्त पद का खोलना।

lessons.title: उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय

blocks.x: जो शब्दांश किसी शब्द के पहले लगकर नया अर्थ पैदा करते हैं उन्हें उपसर्ग कहते हैं, जैसे अ + सत्य = असत्य। जो शब्दांश शब्द के अंत में जुड़ते हैं उन्हें प्रत्यय कहते हैं, जैसे सुंदर + ता = सुंदरता। प्रत्यय के दो भेद हैं: कृदंत और तद्धित।
गहराई से समझें: उपसर्ग
संस्कृत के उपसर्ग: अति, अधि, अनु, अप, अभि, अव, आ, उत्, उप, दुः, निः, परि, प्र, प्रति, वि, सम्, सु। हिंदी के उपसर्ग: अन, अध, उन, कु, नि, भर। उर्दू के उपसर्ग: ला, बे, गैर, ना।
गहराई से समझें: प्रत्यय
कृदंत प्रत्यय क्रिया से बनते हैं: लेख + अक = लेखक, पढ़ + आई = पढ़ाई। तद्धित प्रत्यय संज्ञा/विशेषण से बनते हैं: सुंदर + ता = सुंदरता, धन + वान = धनवान।
Hindi saransh
उपसर्ग शब्द से पहले, प्रत्यय शब्द के बाद।
उपसर्ग = आगे, प्रत्यय = पीछे।

lessons.html:
Visual lesson

उपसर्ग और प्रत्यय

जो शब्दांश किसी शब्द के पहले लगकर नया अर्थ पैदा करते हैं उन्हें उपसर्ग कहते हैं, जैसे अ + सत्य = असत्य। जो शब्दांश शब्द के अंत में जुड़ते हैं उन्हें प्रत्यय कहते हैं…

minutes
formulas
Q&A

1Big idea›2गहराई से समझें: उपसर्ग›3गहराई से समझें: प्रत्यय
🔑

Big idea

  • जो शब्दांश किसी शब्द के पहले लगकर नया अर्थ पैदा करते हैं उन्हें उपसर्ग कहते हैं, जैसे अ + सत्य = असत्य। जो शब्दांश शब्द के अंत में जुड़ते हैं उन्हें…
📌

गहराई से समझें: उपसर्ग

  • संस्कृत के उपसर्ग: अति, अधि, अनु, अप, अभि, अव, आ, उत्, उप, दुः, निः, परि, प्र, प्रति, वि, सम्, सु। हिंदी के उपसर्ग: अन, अध, उन, कु, नि, भर। उर्दू के…
🧠

गहराई से समझें: प्रत्यय

  • कृदंत प्रत्यय क्रिया से बनते हैं: लेख + अक = लेखक, पढ़ + आई = पढ़ाई। तद्धित प्रत्यय संज्ञा/विशेषण से बनते हैं: सुंदर + ता = सुंदरता, धन + वान = धनवान।
🧮

Formula tiles

उपसर्गशब्द के पहलेअ + सत्य = असत्य
प्रत्ययशब्द के बादसुंदर + ता = सुंदरता
प्रत्यय भेदकृदंत, तद्धितदो
उपसर्ग भेदसंस्कृत, हिंदी, उर्दूतीन
🎯 Remember उपसर्ग = आगे, प्रत्यय = पीछे।
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

उपसर्ग शब्द से पहले, प्रत्यय शब्द के बाद।

lessons.title: काल और वाच्य

blocks.x: क्रिया के जिस रूप से कार्य के होने के समय का बोध होता है उसे काल कहते हैं: भूतकाल, वर्तमान काल और भविष्यत् काल। वाच्य क्रिया का वह रूप है जिससे पता चले कि वाक्य में कर्ता, कर्म या भाव प्रधान है। वाच्य तीन प्रकार के हैं: कर्तृवाच्य, कर्मवाच्य और भाववाच्य।
गहराई से समझें: काल

भूतकाल: सामान्य (राम आया), आसन्न (राम आया है), पूर्ण (राम आया था), अपूर्ण (राम आ रहा था), संदिग्ध (राम आया होगा), हेतुहेतुमद् (वह आता तो मैं जाता)। वर्तमान: सामान्य (राम आता है), अपूर्ण (राम आ रहा है), संदिग्ध (राम आता होगा)। भविष्यत्: सामान्य (राम आएगा), संभाव्य (राम आए)।
गहराई से समझें: वाच्य
कर्तृवाच्य: माली पौधे सींचता है। कर्मवाच्य: माली से पौधे सींचे जाते हैं। भाववाच्य: बच्चे से सोया नहीं जाता।
Hindi saransh
काल तीन: भूत, वर्तमान, भविष्यत्। वाच्य तीन: कर्तृ, कर्म, भाव।
वाच्य बदलने में कर्ता के साथ से/द्वारा लगाते हैं।

lessons.title: अलंकार

blocks.x: काव्य की शोभा बढ़ाने वाले तत्त्वों को अलंकार कहते हैं। अलंकार के दो भेद हैं: शब्दालंकार (अनुप्रास, यमक, श्लेष) और अर्थालंकार (उपमा, रूपक, उत्प्रेक्षा, अतिशयोक्ति, मानवीकरण)।
गहराई से समझें: शब्दालंकार
अनुप्रास: तट तमाल तरुवर बहु छाए। यमक: जिस पंक्ति में एक ही शब्द अलग-अलग अर्थ दे। श्लेष: एक शब्द से दो अर्थ चिपके हों।
गहराई से समझें: अर्थालंकार
उपमा: मुख चंद्रमा के समान सुंदर है। रूपक: मुख चंद्रमा है। उत्प्रेक्षा: मुख मानो चंद्रमा है। अतिशयोक्ति में बात बहुत बढ़ाकर कही जाती है, मानवीकरण में प्रकृति मनुष्य जैसी लगती है।
Hindi saransh
अलंकार = काव्य की शोभा। दो भेद: शब्द और अर्थ।
समानता = उपमा, एकरूपता = रूपक, संभावना = उत्प्रेक्षा।

lessons.title: रस

blocks.x: काव्य को पढ़ने-सुनने से जो आनंद मिलता है उसे रस कहते हैं। रस के चार अंग हैं: स्थायी भाव, विभाव, अनुभाव और संचारी भाव। मुख्य रस नौ हैं: शृंगार, हास्य, करुण, रौद्र, वीर, भयानक, वीभत्स, अद्भुत और शांत। वात्सल्य रस दसवाँ माना जाता है।
गहराई से समझें: रस और स्थायी भाव
शृंगार (रति), हास्य (हास), करुण (शोक), रौद्र (क्रोध), वीर (उत्साह), भयानक (भय), वीभत्स (जुगुप्सा), अद्भुत (विस्मय), शांत (निर्वेद)। वात्सल्य रस में सूरदास के बाल-वर्णन प्रसिद्ध हैं।
गहराई से समझें: रस के अंग
आलंबन विभाव वह है जिसके कारण भाव जागे; उद्दीपन विभाव से वह भाव प्रबल होता है; अनुभाव से भाव का बाहरी रूप दिखता है; संचारी भाव कुछ समय के लिए आते-जाते हैं।
Hindi saransh
रस नौ: शृंगार, हास्य, करुण, रौद्र, वीर, भयानक, वीभत्स, अद्भुत, शांत।
स्थायी भाव ही रस बनता है।

lessons.title: मुहावरे और लोकोक्तियाँ

blocks.x: जो वाक्यांश अपने सामान्य अर्थ को छोड़कर विशेष अर्थ देता है उसे मुहावरा कहते हैं, जैसे आँखें खुलना। जो वाक्य लोक में प्रचलित होकर जीवन का अनुभव कहता है उसे लोकोक्ति कहते हैं, जैसे नाच न जाने आँगन टेढ़ा।
गहराई से समझें: मुहावरे
मुहावरे का शब्दार्थ नहीं बल्कि लाक्षणिक अर्थ लिया जाता है। 'चाँदी काटना' का अर्थ खूब लाभ कमाना है। मुहावरे वाक्य में क्रिया के रूप के अनुसार बदलते हैं।
गहराई से समझें: लोकोक्तियाँ
लोकोक्तियाँ अपने आप में पूरा वाक्य होती हैं और जीवन के अनुभव या नीति को कहती हैं। इनका रूप नहीं बदलता।
Hindi saransh
मुहावरा = वाक्यांश, लोकोक्ति = पूरा वाक्य।
मुहावरे का प्रयोग वाक्य के बीच क्रिया के अनुसार बदल जाता है।

मुहावरे और लोकोक्तियाँ

जो वाक्यांश अपने सामान्य अर्थ को छोड़कर विशेष अर्थ देता है उसे मुहावरा कहते हैं, जैसे आँखें खुलना। जो वाक्य लोक में प्रचलित होकर जीवन का अनुभव कहता है उसे लोकोक्ति कहते…

Big idea

📌

गहराई से समझें: मुहावरे

  • मुहावरे का शब्दार्थ नहीं बल्कि लाक्षणिक अर्थ लिया जाता है। 'चाँदी काटना' का अर्थ खूब लाभ कमाना है। मुहावरे वाक्य में क्रिया के रूप के अनुसार बदलते…
🧠

गहराई से समझें: लोकोक्तियाँ

  • लोकोक्तियाँ अपने आप में पूरा वाक्य होती हैं और जीवन के अनुभव या नीति को कहती हैं। इनका रूप नहीं बदलता।
🧮

lessons.title: लेखन: अनुच्छेद, पत्र, सूचना, विज्ञापन, संदेश
yt: class 9 hindi लेखन: अनुच्छेद, पत्र, सूचना, विज्ञापन, संदेश

blocks.x: अनुच्छेद एक विषय पर सुसंगठित वाक्यों का समूह होता है। पत्र दो प्रकार के होते हैं: औपचारिक और अनौपचारिक। सूचना किसी कार्यक्रम की जानकारी देती है, विज्ञापन किसी वस्तु या सेवा का प्रचार करता है और संदेश संक्षेप में बात पहुँचाता है।
गहराई से समझें: पत्र
औपचारिक पत्र में प्रेषक का पता, तिथि, प्रापक, विषय, संबोधन, भाग, समापन होते हैं। अनौपचारिक पत्र में आत्मीय संबोधन (प्रिय मित्र) और स्नेह भरा समापन होता है।
गहराई से समझें: सूचना, विज्ञापन और संदेश
सूचना में संस्था का नाम, 'सूचना' शब्द, तिथि, विषय, कार्यक्रम का स्थान और समय तथा लेखक का नाम-पद लिखते हैं। विज्ञापन में आकर्षक शीर्षक, संक्षिप्त वाक्य और संपर्क होता है। संदेश बॉक्स में लिखा जाता है।
Hindi saransh
लेखन के रूप: अनुच्छेद, पत्र, सूचना, विज्ञापन, संदेश।
पत्र में प्रेषक का पता, तिथि, संबोधन, विषय, मुख्य भाग और समापन होता है।

qa.q: 'अनौपचारिक पत्र' का क्या अर्थ है?
qa.a: परिजन और मित्रों को लिखा पत्र.

lessons.title: अपठित गद्यांश और काव्यांश
yt: class 9 hindi अपठित गद्यांश और काव्यांश

blocks.x: अपठित अंश वह है जो पाठ्यपुस्तक में नहीं पढ़ाया गया हो। इसे ध्यान से दो-तीन बार पढ़ें, मुख्य विचार समझें, प्रश्न पढ़कर उत्तर खोजें और उत्तर अपने शब्दों में लिखें। शीर्षक पूरे अंश का सार बताता है।
गहराई से समझें: रणनीति
पहले पूरा अंश पढ़ें, फिर प्रश्न। जिन शब्दों का अर्थ न आए, प्रसंग से अनुमान लगाएँ। उत्तर संक्षिप्त, पूर्ण और शुद्ध लिखें।
गहराई से समझें: काव्यांश
काव्यांश में पंक्तियों का भावार्थ, प्रयुक्त अलंकार और संदेश पहचानें।
Hindi saransh
अपठित = जो पहले न पढ़ा हो।
पहले अंश पढ़ें, फिर प्रश्न, फिर उत्तर अंश से खोजें।

lessons.title: दो बैलों की कथा
yt: class 9 hindi दो बैलों की कथा

blocks.x: प्रेमचंद की इस कहानी में झूरी काछी के दो बैल हीरा और मोती हैं। दोनों में गहरी मित्रता है। झूरी उन्हें ससुराल भेजता है तो वे स्वतंत्रता और स्वाभिमान के कारण रस्सी तुड़ाकर लौट आते हैं। अंत में वे फिर अपने स्वामी के पास पहुँच जाते हैं। कहानी स्वतंत्रता, मित्रता और अन्याय के विरोध का संदेश देती है।
गहराई से समझें: कथा

झूरी के हीरा-मोती उसे अपने बच्चे जैसे प्रिय थे। गया उन्हें अपने घर ले गया पर वे लौट आए। झूरी ने उनसे प्रेम किया पर गया ने उन्हें फिर पकड़ लिया। उन्हें कम चारा और कठोर व्यवहार मिला। दोनों ने रस्सी तोड़ी, पर पकड़े जाकर कांजीहौस पहुँचे, वहाँ भी उन्होंने साहस दिखाया।
गहराई से समझें: संदेश
कहानी पशु के माध्यम से यह कहती है कि स्वतंत्रता, मित्रता और आत्मसम्मान सबसे बड़े मूल्य हैं। गुलामी स्वीकार करना कायरता है।
Hindi saransh
हीरा-मोती नामक दो बैल स्वतंत्रता और मित्रता का प्रतीक हैं।
गधा सबसे सीधा जानवर माना जाता है, पर बैल उससे भी सीधे हैं।

blocks.x: राहुल सांकृत्यायन का यह यात्रा-वृत्तांत उनकी तिब्बत यात्रा का वर्णन है। वे भिखमंगे का वेश बनाकर ऊँचे दर्रों, डाँड़ों और कठिन रास्तों से होकर ल्हासा की ओर जाते हैं। तिब्बत के गाँव, धर्मशालाएँ, डाकुओं का भय और लोगों का आतिथ्य इसमें वर्णित हैं।
गहराई से समझें: यात्रा

लेखक सुमति के साथ भारत से तिब्बत में प्रवेश करते हैं। रास्ते में ऊँचे डाँड़े, बर्फ़ीली हवा और डाकुओं का भय है। वे गाँवों में ठहरते हैं जहाँ अजनबियों का स्वागत होता है। तिब्बत की चाय, लोगों की सादगी और धार्मिक आस्था का चित्रण होता है।
गहराई से समझें: संदेश
यात्रा-वृत्तांत से ज्ञान की जिज्ञासा, साहस और अनजान संस्कृतियों के प्रति सम्मान की शिक्षा मिलती है।
Hindi saransh

lessons.title: उपभोक्तावाद की संस्कृति

blocks.x: श्यामाचरण दुबे का यह निबंध बताता है कि उपभोक्तावादी संस्कृति में विज्ञापन और बाज़ार के प्रभाव से लोग अधिकाधिक वस्तुएँ खरीदने में सुख मानने लगे हैं। इससे चरित्र, मर्यादा और सामाजिक संबंध प्रभावित हो रहे हैं। लेखक ने सावधान किया है कि यह संस्कृति हमारी सांस्कृतिक अस्मिता के लिए खतरा है।
गहराई से समझें: मुख्य बात
लेखक कहते हैं कि नई उपभोक्ता संस्कृति में भोग ही सुख बन गया है। विज्ञापन लोगों को लगातार नई चीज़ें खरीदने को उकसाते हैं। इससे सादगी, संतोष और सामाजिक संबंध कमज़ोर होते हैं।
गहराई से समझें: चेतावनी
गांधी जी के शब्दों में नई चीज़ें स्वीकारें पर अपनी जड़ें न छोड़ें। उपभोग की इस दौड़ से सामाजिक असंतोष, विषमता और नैतिक पतन बढ़ता है।
Hindi saransh
लेखक उपभोग को ही सुख मानने की प्रवृत्ति के खतरे बताते हैं।
गांधी जी ने कहा था कि हमारे घर की खिड़कियाँ खुली रहें पर हम उड़ न जाएँ।

lessons.title: साँवले सपनों की याद
yt: class 9 hindi साँवले सपनों की याद

blocks.x: जाबिर हुसैन का यह संस्मरणात्मक निबंध प्रसिद्ध पक्षी-विज्ञानी सालिम अली को श्रद्धांजलि है। उनकी मृत्यु पर लेखक पक्षियों, प्रकृति और सालिम अली के जीवन से जुड़ी यादों को याद करते हैं। सालिम अली प्रकृति-प्रेमी और संवेदनशील व्यक्ति थे।
गहराई से समझें: विषय
लेखक सालिम अली के निधन से उदास हैं और उनके पक्षी-प्रेम, प्रकृति के प्रति संवेदना और सादगी को याद करते हैं। वे बताते हैं कि सालिम अली ने पक्षियों की दुनिया को समझा और मनुष्य को प्रकृति से जोड़ा।
गहराई से समझें: संदेश
पाठ हमें प्रकृति के प्रति संवेदनशील होने और पर्यावरण की रक्षा करने की प्रेरणा देता है।
Hindi saransh
सालिम अली पक्षियों से प्रेम करने वाले महान पक्षी-विज्ञानी थे।
सालिम अली को भारत का पक्षी-पुरुष (बर्डमैन) कहा जाता है।

blocks.x: चपला देवी द्वारा लिखित यह पाठ 1857 के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम के दौरान नाना साहब की बेटी मैना के बलिदान का वर्णन करता है। अंग्रेज़ों ने बिठूर में मैना को पकड़कर जला दिया। उसकी वीरता और देशभक्ति अमर है।
गहराई से समझें: घटना
1857 के संग्राम में अंग्रेज़ों ने बिठूर पर आक्रमण किया। नाना साहब बच निकले पर उनकी पुत्री मैना पकड़ी गई। उसने अंग्रेज़ों के सामने निर्भीकता दिखाई और उसे जला दिया गया।
गहराई से समझें: संदेश
पाठ बलिदानियों के प्रति सम्मान सिखाता है। मैना का बलिदान प्रेरणा है।
Hindi saransh
मैना ने अंग्रेज़ों के अत्याचार का साहस से सामना किया।
1857 के संग्राम में नाना साहब प्रमुख नेता थे।
